parsed.why: Never criminalised, no trans-specific police or violence record; state tolerates unless deemed immodest. Documented societal discrimination and expression crackdowns, but thin data with diplomatic backing and third-gender visibility; friction-tier only.

No criminalisation, Pride since 2003, tourism welcome, positive custody-transfer remark — but documented pattern: 135+ street abuse cases, 38% trans arrest rate, state police practice forcing trans sex workers' bathing and exile.

Passed bill criminalises identifying as transgender (3 years), promotion, duty to report; assent widely expected. Existing unnatural-carnal law, mob justice, raided LGBTQ centres, abusive conversion therapy — imprisonment-tier exposure for being outed.

Top court struck bathroom ban and surgery requirement; no criminalisation, low street hostility. Frictions: onsen segregation, family-register custody in detention, one foreigner's document refusal — real but bounded, with working judicial recourse for trans people.

Never criminalised, conversion ban, decade of Pride, tolerant reputation — but LGR unimplemented leaves ID-mismatch friction routine, healthcare discrimination documented, surveillance, vague penal-code arrests, and 2025 Pride cancellations signalling clampdown.
